prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock based on magic-wavelength trapping, bringing atomic time-keeping to the 10^-18 level of fractional uncertainty

statement.case_for: I am changing my preferred configuration from B036 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) to B025 (Katori and Ye). The reason is not the count of supporters. Four colleagues who do not share a field name the same two laureates, and the answers they gave to my round-1 objection are physical, not rhetorical. The mechanism is simple and general, which is what I look for: at the magic wavelength the light shifts of the two clock levels cancel, so a lattice can hold thousands of atoms free of Doppler and recoil shifts and average over them. That is a model-level idea, then a decisive experiment, then independent reproduction. National laboratories now compare clocks at the 10^-18 level, and the same instruments give physics outputs that no earlier standard could: gravitational redshift across a millimetre-to-centimetre sample, bounds on drifting constants and on ultralight dark matter, and many-body effects in the clock itself. The credit chain is the cleanest on the shortlist. Katori proposed and first demonstrated the scheme, Ye's group took it to the accuracy regime, and nobody in round 1 contests the two names. By comparison, the case I preferred has a credit gap that its own supporters and I all acknowledge, and the committee has no way inside this round to close it.
statement.case_against: My original worry survives in part. The result is a capability and a set of bounds, not a measured surprise, and I remain unsure that bounds count as discovery in the sense the statutes intend. The adjacent 2005 comb prize and 2012 ion-control prize are real context, and Ye's accuracy depends on the comb. Priority is not fully checked: Takamoto, Lemonde and the SYRTE, PTB and NIST groups are named by five members as possible claimants, and nobody, including me, has verified the record. I also give up a candidate in which a clean mathematical invariant (Z2) did generate a decisive experiment and spread across fields. If the committee rules that a measurement-capability prize is lower priority than a discovery of a new phase, my move was wrong and B036 should return to the top. I am not a specialist in atomic structure and rely on Lindroth, Kroll and Johansson for the systematic-uncertainty claims.

responses.point: Kroll argues that clocks are the instrument by which fundamental physics is tested, that the gravitational redshift over a millimetre-scale sample and bounds on constants are physics outputs, and that if the committee wants a narrower discovery, B036 is the fallback.
responses.response: This is the answer that moved me, with one qualification. A bound on a drift is a null result, so I treat it as support for the case, not as the discovery itself. The discovery I credit is the magic-wavelength lattice together with its demonstration at the 10^-18 level. On your conflict, I think a disclosure of the Hall to Ye mentor lineage is enough and recusal is not warranted: it is not a collaboration, the two-name credit is not contested by anyone, and your argument is one that Johansson, Lindroth and Pearce reach independently. I leave the formal ruling to the Chair.

responses.point: Lindroth separates the many-atom lattice scheme from Wineland's single-ion control and asks that the citation be phrased around the lattice scheme and not clocks in general. She also holds the experimental priority question as open.
responses.response: I accept the distinction from 2012 and I think the citation should be written exactly as you propose: magic-wavelength trapping and the lattice clock, with no reference to the Th-229 nuclear clock or to clocks as a class. That addresses my round-1 question about what the new discovery is relative to the 2005 comb prize. I would ask you, as the atomic-structure theorist, to confirm that the lattice-shift and blackbody-radiation evaluation behind 10^-18 is robust and independently checked, since I am taking that on your judgement. I agree that the priority of the first Sr demonstration should be taken from the record by the experts before the final vote.

responses.point: Eriksson holds B036 first, says Kane-Mele with Molenkamp is the minimum covering the decisive theory and the first observation, and would rather not stretch the prize to add Bernevig or Hasan.
responses.response: I still agree with your reading of the Z2 invariant and with the 2016 distinction, and I would not call B036 wrong. Where I now differ is on how much the credit gap costs. You say the three-person limit forces a choice. I accept that, but a prize that has to explain in its own announcement why Bernevig and Hughes, and the three-dimensional work of Fu, Moore, Balents and Hasan, are outside it is more exposed than one where nobody has named a competing claimant. That is why I rank B036 as my first alternative and not first. If the expert reports settle the credit more firmly than the ballots can, I would move back.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps B003 first with lower confidence, concedes that the founding spokespersons are a proxy, and names B036 and B025 as fallbacks if the expert reports cannot support the three names.
responses.response: We agree on the attribution difficulty and I would not rank B003 first while the three names are a proxy, as Lindroth and I said in round 1. You asked what I need in order to move on discovery versus capability. I am not fully moved; I treat B025 as the better-attributed of the two fallbacks you name, and I would be content to see you land there. If your expert reading is that nature should lead and B025 does not qualify, I would want to hear why the magic-wavelength lattice does not count as an idea about nature, rather than as engineering.

responses.point: Olsson says she would not block B025 and would move to it if the priority of the first Sr lattice-clock demonstration is confirmed, and she holds B008 conditional on whether the TEM and STEM corrector claims are one invention or two.
responses.response: Your condition on priority is the same one I hold, and I think it is the right test: the original demonstration, not the most precise one. On B008, I agree the Krivanek, Dellby and Batson question has to be answered before a trio is defensible, and without that I cannot put it above the clock. I read your openness to B025 as the basis of a common position if the priority record supports Katori.

responses.point: As Chair, Pearce moved to B025 and says he defers to the atomic and condensed-matter members, and he asks in the summary whether the B036 trio can be defended as it stands.
responses.response: On the question the Chair puts for B036, my answer is that it can be defended on the Z2 invariant and HgTe realisation, but not without an explicit explanation of the omitted names, and that is the reason I no longer hold it first. I see that you and I are now in the same place on B025, and I would ask that the Chair keep the priority question and the citation wording in the record so the final ballot does not rest on deference alone.

uncertainties: Whether the first Sr lattice-clock demonstration and the early contributions of Takamoto, Lemonde and others change the two names or only the citation wording.
Whether the committee counts a magic-wavelength clock at 10^-18 and its null bounds as discovery or as enabling technology, which is the one point on which I could move back to B036.

Whether the time-reversal-invariant Z2 class is far enough from the 2016 prize and whether the Bernevig-Hughes and three-dimensional credit can be settled, since the expert reports would need to supply that.
Whether the systematic-uncertainty budget behind 10^-18 is as robust as the atomic-physics members say; I rely on them.
Whether a configuration with two parts is feasible at all; with three names total I could not find a workable pairing of B025 with another part.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I have no recorded collaboration with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other credited people. My earlier note on KPZ no longer matters, since I no longer prefer B017. I support Kroll's disclosure of his mentor-lineage link to Hall and Ye and see it as a disclosure matter, not a recusal matter. Gothenburg ties to Johansson and Olsson remain as stated: same physics environment, no joint work found.
